risk_if_not_implemented: Without Sharing Identification & Authentication Information, credentials may be phished, replayed, guessed or stolen, allowing unauthorized actors to authenticate as trusted identities. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Accountability / Attribution (R-AC-1), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Lack of oversight of third-party controls (R-GV-7), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Personnel Security
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to control personnel security requirements including security roles and responsibilities for third-party providers.
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Personnel Security (TPM-13) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Sharing Identification & Authentication Information (IAC-36.1) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
compensating_control_2.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for:
(1) Remote network access; 
(2) Third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and/ or
(3) Non-console access to critical TAAS that store, transmit and/or process sensitive and/or regulated data.
compensating_control_2.justification: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) (IAC-37) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Sharing Identification & Authentication Information (IAC-36.1) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
